blocks.text:
I’m a dog-eared page
You read too fast
Folded where
The feeling passed

Coffee ring
Around a word
Something true
You never heard

Highlighter bled
Through borrowed hands
Meant more
Than they had planned

Boxed with things
That fit the shelf
Not the part
That felt like hell
spoken aside, piano drops to single notes

No bell rang
No names were said
No one mourned
What wasn’t dead

Just a mark
Where someone stood
And meant it
For good
(piano repeats opening figure, softer each time)

notebook.style: Dusty late-night jazz ballad set in a smoke-filled basement bar at 2am, Sparse, out-of-tune upright piano with heavy felt hammers; slow, swaying tempo, minor key, unresolved harmonies, Lots of space between notes—silence is part of the rhythm, No drums or very minimal brushed texture, if any, Subtle room noise allowed (glass clink, pedal creak, breath), Vocals are close-mic, intimate, almost spoken; restrained and weary rather than dramatic, Consonants clear, pitch secondary to phrasing, Lines often arrive slightly behind the beat, Emotional tone is quiet grief, resignation, and witness—no catharsis, no uplift, Overall feel: a song overheard, not performed, Feels like it existed before the listener arrived and will continue after they leave, End unresolved, piano pedal down, no clean finish
